t.5.23.1: As those grim rākṣasīs spoke thus, uttering many harsh and dreadful things, Janaka's daughter wept.
t.5.23.2: Thus addressed by the rākṣasīs, the high-minded Vaidehī, utterly terrified, spoke in a voice choked with tears.
t.5.23.3: A human woman cannot become the wife of a rākṣasa. Devour me if you wish, all of you; I will not do as you say.
t.5.23.5: Sītā trembled all the more, as though shrinking into her own body, like a doe in the forest separated from her herd and harried by wolves.
t.5.23.4: Sītā, like a daughter of the gods, standing amid the rākṣasīs, afflicted with sorrow and threatened by Rāvaṇa, found no peace.
t.5.23.6: But she, her heart broken, took hold of a broad, blossoming branch of the aśoka tree and, overcome with sorrow, thought of her husband.
t.5.23.7: Bathing her full breasts with streams of tears from her eyes and lost in thought, she then found no end to her sorrow.
t.5.23.8: Trembling, ready to fall like a plantain tree in a strong wind, she, stricken with fear of the rākṣasīs, became pale of face.
t.5.23.9: As she trembled, that long and thick braid of Sītā's was then seen quivering, like a female serpent gliding along.
t.5.23.10: Sighing deeply, afflicted with sorrow, her mind stricken by grief, the distressed Maithilī shed tears and lamented.
t.5.23.11: Stricken with grief, she cried, "Alas, Rāma!" and again, "Alas, Lakṣmaṇa!" and "Alas, Kausalyā, my mother-in-law! Alas, noble Sumitrā!"
t.5.23.13: Since here, tormented by these cruel rākṣasīs, I live on in sorrow, bereft of Rāma, even for a single moment.
t.5.23.12: True is this popular saying, declared by the learned: death before its appointed time is hard to obtain, whether for a woman or for a man.
t.5.23.14: I, of little merit and wretched, shall perish like one without a protector, like a laden ship in the midst of the ocean struck by the force of the winds.
t.5.23.15: Not seeing that husband of mine, and fallen into the power of the rākṣasīs, I sink down indeed with grief, like a riverbank battered by the waters.
t.5.23.16: Fortunate are those who behold my lord, whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus, who walks with the stride of a lion, who is grateful and gentle of speech.
t.5.23.17: Bereft in every way of that Rāma whose self is known, my life is hard to sustain, like one who has tasted a sharp poison.
t.5.23.18: What kind of sin did I commit long ago in another body, by which this terrible, exceedingly cruel sorrow is now being suffered by me?
t.5.23.20: Fie upon human existence, and fie upon being subject to the will of another, since one cannot cast away one's life by one's own choice!
t.5.23.19: Overwhelmed by great sorrow, I wish to give up my life; guarded as I am by the rākṣasīs, Rāma cannot be reached by me.
